summary: Same core Knizia puzzle as the original Ingenious: place tiles to extend lines of matching colored symbols, and your score is capped by your weakest color, forcing balanced play instead of specialization. The 3D layering adds a spatial twist where tiles can stack, opening new scoring lines but also adding a bit of visual clutter and analysis time compared to the flat original.
praised: Retains the elegant, easy-to-teach 'score your worst color' mechanism that makes the base game a classic
Stacking/layering adds a fresh spatial puzzle layer for fans of the original
Quick to learn, scales well from 1-4 players
criticised: 3D tiles can be fiddly to place and see clearly compared to a flat board
Feels like a reskin/variant rather than a substantially new game to those who already own Ingenious
Some prefer the cleaner, faster flat original over the added physical complexity

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial via shared board space

scoring.why: The winner is whoever best balances scoring across all colors, since the final score is your lowest color total, not your sum.
